situated_beneficiary.person_or_government: The government in office on 12 February 1991 (as to who may be appointed minister or deputy minister during the Twelfth Knesset) and the members of the Twelfth Knesset who had left their factions before the law's commencement (identifiable from Knesset records)
situated_beneficiary.matter: Eligibility of pre-commencement defectors to serve as ministers (new s. 5(b1) of Basic Law: The Government) or deputy ministers (new s. 34(b)) and to stand again (new s. 6A of Basic Law: The Knesset), and the validity of agreements made with them on their departure
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 4: a single-instance transitional clause in the enactment itself, s. 6 (הוראת מעבר), confined to 'the Twelfth Knesset' and to members who left their factions 'before the commencement of this law': (a)(1) exempts Twelfth-Knesset faction splits from the agreement-filing condition if notice is given within three months; (a)(2) lets members who had already left join a split group and be treated as having split; (a)(3) voids every agreement made with a member who left before commencement and returned (or returns within six months) and deems him never to have left, so the new bars on ministerial and deputy-ministerial office do not reach him; (b) adjusts party financing accordingly
situated_beneficiary.source: Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 12), gazette text, ס"ח תשנ"א 1345, pp. 90-93 (Knesset PDF 12_lsr_210826.pdf via web.archive.org capture 2021-05-12)

situated_beneficiary.list_version: (ae), adopted 2026-10-22, as clarified by (af) the same day
situated_beneficiary.note: Second pass on the whole law as passed 18 March 1992. Read all 65 sections: direct election of the prime minister (ss. 3-15), eligibility of ministers including the defector bars (ss. 16, 37(c)), publication and limits of agreements (ss. 17-18), no confidence by a majority of members and dissolution on no confidence or failure to pass the budget (ss. 19-21), dissolution by the prime minister (s. 22), resignation, investigation, removal, incapacity and acting prime minister (ss. 23-32), ministers and deputy ministers (ss. 33-38), powers, secrecy, emergency (ss. 39-55), entrenchment (s. 56), indirect amendments (ss. 57-62), repeal of the 1968 law, commencement (s. 63), emergency transitional (s. 64), publication (s. 65). Every provision is general in form; the only transitional clauses are s. 63 (application from the Fourteenth Knesset elections) and s. 64 (state of emergency deemed declared at commencement). Nothing names the Twelfth Knesset, the government then in office, or any officeholder; no fixed deadline binding the sitting government or an officeholder is moved; no single-instance or sunset clause attaches to the sitting government's measure or term. The Twelfth Knesset's own dissolution law was under plenary debate on 4 February 1992 (NYU mirror of the Knesset record, handle 2451/70522), but a pending Knesset bill is not an item of the closed list. Items 1 and 2 searched: press reports of January-March 1992 (Christian Science Monitor 17 and 21 January 1992; JTA items of 3 and 10 January 1992 via the Bentley Detroit Jewish News archive; a chronology entry dated 18 March 1992 recording passage) and any petition or formal step pending on 18 March 1992 against the government, a minister or a coalition agreement; none found. Likud's and Shamir's opposition to the bill is a political fact, not a closed-list item, and motive was not used.
